doc_verification.detail: Reachability: page fetched via MCP web reader (title 'Collect cluster telemetry data | Qdrant | API Reference'); the WebFetch tool itself was network-blocked for api.qdrant.tech — reachability established through the alternate reader, recorded honestly. Version: page is under /v-1-18-x/ and displays v1.18.x; target v1.18.0 major.minor match. Content: doc states GET /cluster/telemetry; query parameters details_level integer Optional and timeout integer Optional '>=1' Defaults to '60' — verbatim match with the contract's range unit 'timeout default 60, minimum 1'; documented success is '200 Retrieved' with the distributed telemetry payload (example shows a single-peer cluster: cluster.enabled=true, number_of_peers:1) — matching the behavioral unit's 'returns 200'; NO standalone/distributed-mode precondition or any 5xx is documented for this endpoint. Minor note: the contract's field enumeration for the behavioral unit (id, app, collections, cluster, requests, memory, hardware, search_pool, quota) blends the separate /telemetry (service) response; the load-bearing claim 'HTTP 200 success' matches the page exactly. Endpoint precision: observed requests (timeout matrix {omitted,1,2,60,0,-1,-100} on GET /cluster/telemetry) match the registry entry cluster+telemetry GET with params details_level/timeout exactly.

http_semantics.note: Primary observation is a server-side 5xx on fully valid documented requests — not a masked client error. The request-side-decidable legs behaved correctly: timeout=0 -> HTTP 422 with field-level validation text; timeout=-1/-100 -> HTTP 400 with deserialize text.

contract_grounding.detail_note: assertion_text_quoted is the verbatim description field of qdrant_behavioral_cluster_telemetry_001 in structured_contract.json (line 7623); the same unit's expected_behavior field reads verbatim: "HTTP 200 with telemetry payload (id, app, collections, cluster, requests, memory, hardware, search_pool, quota)". Dispatched constraint_id was EMPTY (see chain_trace); the observed phenomenon (500 on every valid form, including the documented default-omitted form) grounds on this behavioral unit, whose documented domain covers all observed request forms — no domain mismatch. violates=true is chosen on the 'genuinely violates' branch: the value domain is irrelevant here because the failure is unconditional (source: empty peer map in standalone), so this is not the 'accepted-but-compliant' branch. Co-anchor context: the script's in-log quote (log line 5) cites qdrant_range_cluster_telemetry_001 (assertion verbatim: "timeout default 60, minimum 1"), and that range face was NOT violated (422 on 0, 400 on -1/-100).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: GET /cluster/telemetry (actix route, cluster_api.rs:203) -> get_cluster_telemetry -> channel_service.id_to_address.keys() (cluster_api.rs:238-243). In standalone deployments (ClusterConfig.enabled=false, disabled by default per settings.rs:117; deployment_meta.json confirms stock qdrant/qdrant:v1.18.0 container 'testvdb-qdrant-standalone'), init_channel_service (main.rs:299-316) only fills id_to_address when is_distributed_deployment, so the map is empty (channel_service.rs:47). all_peers is therefore empty -> zero gRPC GetTelemetry futures -> telemetries stays empty (the 0.2-3.4 ms response times in the log corroborate that no peer was ever contacted) -> resolve_telemetries (distributed_telemetry.rs:157-158) -> newest_telemetry over an empty vec returns None -> StorageError::service_error("Could not get telemetry from cluster") -> helpers.rs:247 maps ServiceError to HTTP 500. Conclusion: the 500 is DETERMINISTIC and parameter-independent on every standalone deployment for every valid request form, including the documented default-omitted form. Separately, the timeout range face is fully conformant: #[validate(range(min=1))] at cluster_api.rs:45 produced the observed 422 on timeout=0; negatives fail serde (400); the omitted default is DEFAULT_GRPC_TIMEOUT=60s (transport_channel_pool.rs:25), matching the documented 'default 60'. No standalone guard exists on this handler — contrast /cluster/recover (toc/mod.rs:563,778: explicit 'Qdrant is running in standalone mode') and GET /cluster (works, reports status 'disabled').
source_grounding.outcome_qualification: Two faces must be distinguished. Range face (qdrant_range_cluster_telemetry_001, the script's self-quoted constraint): validation PRESENT in source (range(min=1), cluster_api.rs:45) and observed enforced (422/400) — NOT violated. Behavioral face (qdrant_behavioral_cluster_telemetry_001, the violated unit): the handling the contract requires (HTTP 200 with telemetry payload) is ABSENT for standalone deployments — no guard, no local-telemetry fallback; the endpoint unconditionally 500s via the empty-peer-map path. by_design_in_source was considered and REJECTED: the only nearby comments are main.rs:300 'We only need channel_service in case if cluster is enabled' (explains channel-service initialization, expresses no intent about /cluster/telemetry's standalone disposition) and cluster_api.rs:23-24 'TODO(cluster telemetry): Handle lower levels' (about details_level, not standalone); neither is an explicit design declaration for the observed 500, and the API reference documents 200 (single-peer example) with no cluster-mode precondition.

excluded: env malfunction: deployment is the stock qdrant/qdrant:v1.18.0 container in its DEFAULT configuration (cluster disabled by default, settings.rs:117); /healthz 200 and GET /cluster 200 in the same window prove the server healthy; the failing code path performs no network I/O (empty peer map), so this is not a sandbox/networking artifact
request-parameter typo: route and parameters match the documented endpoint exactly (log line 3 [url-derived] cluster+telemetry -> /cluster/telemetry)
concurrency race / cache delay: deterministic sub-4 ms responses, identical 500 across 13/13 scripts spanning boundary/semantic/state attack families
mundane_explanation.surviving: deployment-mode scoping: the 'returns 200 TelemetryData' contract is violated specifically on standalone (cluster disabled = the DEFAULT) deployments; the doc's own 200 example shows a 1-peer cluster and imposes no cluster-mode precondition, and same-family endpoints handle standalone explicitly (GET /cluster -> 200 status:'disabled'; POST /cluster/recover -> explicit 'Qdrant is running in standalone mode'), so no source or doc basis currently marks the telemetry 500 as intended — but whether the maintainer deems this ops endpoint standalone-out-of-scope is an undocumented judgment call left to the adjudicator. Secondary surviving observation (Type2 flavor, not the primary claim): the 500's message 'Could not get telemetry from cluster' misattributes the cause — no cluster contact was ever attempted.
